title: Coffee Mousse
subtitle: Espresso-dark mousse of eggs, sugar, and cream
excerpt: A proper egg-based mousse with a strong espresso flavour, yolks beaten over heat until thick, espresso folded through, then cream and beaten egg whites to lighten. Needs a bain-marie and careful timing.
sourceNotes: Coffee mousse follows the same construction as classic chocolate mousse, substituting espresso for the melted chocolate. The egg-yolk sabayon base, beaten over a bain-marie with sugar until thick and pale, gives the mousse its characteristic richness and lifts the espresso into something more refined than a cream-and-coffee blend.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to a day ahead and keep covered in the fridge. The mousse firms a little on day two.

content.text: Coffee mousse is made the same way as chocolate mousse. Beat egg yolks with sugar over a bain-marie until thick and pale. Fold in espresso, then whipped cream, then stiff egg whites. The result is light and airy with a strong coffee hit.

items.prepNote: melted and cooled, optional, for a mocha version

content.text: Pour 3 cm of water into a medium saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer. Place a large heatproof bowl over the pan, the base should not touch the water. Add the egg yolks and caster sugar to the bowl and beat with a hand mixer on medium speed for 8 to 10 minutes until the mixture is very pale, thick, and ribbony, when you lift the beaters, the mixture should autumn in a thick ribbon that holds for a moment on the surface. Remove from the heat and continue beating for 2 minutes until slightly cooled. The bowl will be hot, handle with a cloth.

Fold the cooled espresso into the sabayon, use 3 shots (about 90ml) for a strong result. If making the mocha version, fold in the cooled melted dark chocolate at this stage. Leave to cool to room temperature.

In a clean bowl, whip the double cream to soft peaks. In a separate clean, dry bowl, whisk the egg whites to firm, glossy peaks. Fold the whipped cream into the coffee sabayon, then fold in the egg whites in two additions, using a large metal spoon and slow sweeping movements. Stop as soon as the mixture is uniform. Divide between glasses or ramekins and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

items.cause: The water was simmering too vigorously and the bowl overheated.
items.fix: The water should be a bare simmer, steam rising but no visible bubbling. If the bowl feels very hot to touch, lift it off the heat for 30 seconds while continuing to beat.

items.cause: The egg whites were over-folded, or the cream was whipped to stiff rather than soft peaks.
items.fix: Fold the egg whites with a light touch and stop at the first sign of uniformity. Over-mixing knocks out the air built up during whisking.

items.cause: The espresso was weak or the shots were small.
items.fix: Use 3 full shots from a moka pot or espresso machine. Let the espresso cool fully before adding, a warm espresso will deflate the sabayon.

content.text: Best eaten the same day. Keeps covered in the fridge for up to 24 hours; the mousse firms and the coffee flavour deepens. Do not freeze.
